Use case: identity-preserve
Asset type: directional sprite turnaround for the existing French sci-fi roguelike Project RL, authored with crisp painted pixel art at 64 pixels per ground tile.
Image 1 is the canonical in-game design and palette, and its mild top view is the camera reference. Small ivory hovering scout, wide compact center pod and two symmetric side thrusters, cyan scanner only on its front, cyan nozzles underneath. The back has the same pod and thruster silhouettes, a subtle dark service panel, no cyan rectangular front eye. No legs.
Output exactly FOUR separate complete sprites, in a regular 2 by 2 grid of equally sized square cells with generous transparent gutters: TOP LEFT true leftward side with nose pointing left; TOP RIGHT true rightward side with nose pointing right; BOTTOM LEFT true front with nose/sensors pointing toward the viewer, mild top view; BOTTOM RIGHT true rear with nose pointed away and back plates facing viewer, mild top view. Each view depicts the exact same physical chassis and attachments from that new direction. Floor axes parallel to screen axes, no isometric projection. Match materials, existing asymmetric parts and silhouette. Same neutral contact stance and overall native scale in every cell. Put each sprite in the center of its own quadrant with 15% transparent margin. No text, arrows, dividers, labels, backdrop, contact shadow, flashes, glow cloud, or effects. Genuine transparent background. Strong small pixel clusters with matte metal, no smooth gradients.
